Hi Sara — thanks for sending this over and for the checklist, very clear.

Short answers up front:
- EU-only processing: Yes — we operate a customer-configurable in-region processing policy. For MediHealth we will enforce EU-only compute and persistent storage. The control plane metadata (account IDs, billing usage) is stored in a separate control plane which can be configured to the EU control plane; we will scope this for you in the contract.
- Deletion: primary data is removed immediately upon a deletion request; caches and KV prefixes are invalidated synchronously. Backups are retained by default for disaster recovery (see details below) but can be configured to a shorter retention and we offer an attestation for deletion.
- SCCs: We provide the EU Commission SCCs (module 2) as part of our standard DPA and maintain a register of subprocessors; Naomi will follow up on flow-down language.

Sara — copied from the thread above. A few legal clarifications on SCCs and flow-downs: 

1) SCCs + supplementary measures: Redwood executes the latest EU Commission SCCs for controller-processor/controler-subprocessor relationships as applicable. For customers requiring additional measures under Schrems II considerations, we offer documented technical measures (encryption at rest with customer-managed keys in EU KMS, strict in-region processing, and strict egress controls) that together constitute our supplementary measures. We will include these in the DPA exhibit.

2) Flow-downs: Redwood maintains a public subprocessors list and will accept limited flow-down language for core data processing obligations. Exceptions: we cannot accept unlimited indemnity for downstream subprocessors; we will propose a negotiated paragraph that requires prior notice and approval for any new EU-impacting subprocessor.

3) Evidence & attestation: We can provide an operational attestation (signed by our Security and Legal) showing deletion timelines and a sample deletion certificate for a test deletion. For high-assurance customers we support scheduled deletion audits (limited scope).

4) Backup deletion: backups are a secondary copy; our standard is to expire and purge backup snapshots on a rolling schedule. We can provide a retention window and a purge timeline, and for contractually required shorter windows we will commit to an SLA with an attestation process.

Please mark any questionnaire items that are 'must have' vs 'nice to have' and I will circulate a DPA exhibit with proposed language.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — operational details below (high level) to plug into the questionnaire. Happy to walk through live if useful.

Primary storage: deletion request triggers immediate tombstone in the primary dataset. Logical deletion acknowledged to the customer within seconds; physical reclaim of storage occurs on the next garbage-collection cycle (within 24 hours for object store; within 48 hours for DB segments where compaction is required).

Caches & KV: KV cache entries and edge caches are invalidated synchronously. Any in-memory caches are flushed; we surface cache invalidation events in logs.

Backups: 
- Snapshot retention default: 90 days.
- Configurable lower retention: we can set per-customer snapshot retention to 30 days at contract time for MediHealth.
- Backup purge process: snapshots marked for purge are queued; secure deletion from object storage begins within 7 days of purge and typically completes within 30 days of purge start.

Key management: for customers who opt for customer-managed keys (EU KMS), key rotation and destruction controls are available. If a key is destroyed, data encrypted with that key becomes unrecoverable (effective cryptographic shredding).

Proof of deletion / attestation: we can provide a signed Certificate of Deletion that references the deletion request ID, affected object IDs, GC window, and backup purge batch IDs. For MediHealth we propose the following SLA: Certificate issued within 10 business days of final purge completion (final purge = backups fully purged per selected retention).

Attached a diagram that shows the backup purge pipeline and logpoints.

Cheers,
